blocks.text: What policy analysts build in PowerPoint on Mac

Most policy analysts use PowerPoint for three jobs. You brief a minister or a director. You present to a committee. You send a short deck to a partner who reads it alone. Each job needs a different look, so start by naming the job.

A briefing deck is short and direct. Each slide makes one claim, and each chart carries a source line at the bottom. A committee deck runs longer and holds more tables. A reader deck must make sense with no speaker in the room.
Build your master for the longest version of this work, then copy it for the rest. That habit saves more time than any single shortcut.
Set up one slide master before you write a slide
A slide master controls the fonts, colors, logo and footer on every slide in a deck. Set it once and you stop fixing fonts by hand. Microsoft's Mac steps are simple, and they start on the View tab.

items: Open View > Slide Master. The Slide Master tab appears across the top.
Click the top master slide. Set the title font, body font, theme colors and your department logo here.
Choose Slide Master tab > Insert Slide Master to add a second master, for example one for memos or one-page notes.
Set the size and orientation with Slide Master tab > Slide Size > Page Setup before you add any content.
Click Close Master when you finish. Then choose File > Save as Template to keep a reusable copy.

blocks.text: Microsoft's Mac steps list no keyboard shortcut for Slide Master. Use the menu. Lists of third-party shortcuts exist, but test any shortcut on your own Mac before you trust it.

blocks.title: Set the master before you paste
blocks.text: Pasted text can keep its old fonts and colors. Set the master first, then use the paste options to match the destination theme.
Designer and custom templates: the 15-layout rule
Designer is the PowerPoint feature that suggests layouts for a slide. Microsoft sets clear limits for custom templates. Each slide master needs at least 15 layouts before Designer supports it.
Designer only suggests layouts from the master that a slide uses. So keep related layouts in one master. Do not spread briefing layouts across three masters and expect Designer to mix them.
Two limits matter most for analysts. Designer does not yet suggest designs for slides with tables or charts. It also does not support animations or OLE objects on the master or its layouts.

headers: What it means for your deck
rows: Build the full set, even if you only use a few. Designer counts them.
One master per family of slides
Keep briefing layouts together so Designer suggests from the right set.
Designer skips these slides. Lay them out by hand.
Animations or OLE objects on the master
Keep them on individual slides, not on the master or its layouts.

blocks.text: Charts and tables: lay them out by hand
Charts and tables carry most of the evidence in a policy deck. Designer leaves those slides alone, so you own their layout. A fixed order keeps the rework down.

Here is a worked example. You build a short brief with a title slide, an executive summary, a spending chart and an options table. The summary uses a title and content layout. The chart and the table use a title only layout, with the source line in the master footer, so it appears on every slide without retyping.
Avoid pasting a chart as a picture. A picture cannot update when the data changes, and nobody can check its numbers. Keep the chart as a chart, or keep the source workbook open beside the deck.
SVG graphics from your stats tool on Mac
Many analysts make charts in other tools and export them as SVG files. PowerPoint for Mac 16.13 and later supports SVG. That support matters if your stats tool exports only vector files.
Microsoft's release notes say that on March 10, 2026, build 16.107 stopped saving a PNG fallback next to each SVG graphic in .pptx files. That changes what older versions can show.
Test before you send. Open the file on a colleague's Mac with an older version. The release notes do not say what older versions display, so do not assume the graphic will appear.
SmartArt for process flows and approval chains

Process flows, approval chains and consultation timelines suit SmartArt. Open it from Insert > SmartArt, pick a process layout and type into the boxes. Use it for short flows where each step has only a few words. Long sentences break the boxes.
Printing and PDF handouts from a Mac

Check the printed copy before the meeting, not on the morning of it. Microsoft's known-issues page lists printing problems in the web versions of Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Test your own Mac and printer on a single page first.

Press ⌘P to open the print dialog. Choose the PDF option in the print dialog and save the file. Send that file to reviewers. A PDF shows the pages as you saved them, and readers cannot change it by accident.
Known issues and reduced functionality mode on Mac

Microsoft's known-issues page says that starting July 13, 2026, some Mac users may find Office apps, including PowerPoint, can open and print files but not edit or save them. The notice covers Microsoft 365 subscribers on macOS, and non-subscription Office 2021 or 2019 on macOS.
If your deck will not save, check that page before you change anything. The same page lists export to video problems on some Macs as mitigated.
I did not verify whether the July 13 notice is still in effect in November 2026. Read the page on the day you work, and ask your IT team if your Mac cannot save.

blocks.title: Sensitivity labels and language
blocks.text: Microsoft lists sensitivity label policies that may not apply in PowerPoint for Mac when the language is not en-US. If your Mac uses another language, check each label by hand before you send.
Copilot in PowerPoint on Mac: what it adds

Microsoft added Copilot in PowerPoint to Mac Office in version 16.109 on May 12, 2026. It edits a presentation from plain language requests. Microsoft says the feature is available with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic). Premium adds a brand kit, branded templates, brand-approved images and brand compliance checks.
Copilot and Lazur do different jobs. Copilot edits the deck. Lazur answers questions, points at things and guides you through steps. It does not click buttons or edit files for you.
A third-party summary of Microsoft's research quotes Microsoft saying generated presentations should be reviewed by a person. Plan time to check every claim, number and chart that a tool writes.
How much time do these tools actually save?

Vendor numbers look large, so read them closely before you quote one to a director. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index reports a 122% spike in PowerPoint view and edit actions in the final 10 minutes before a meeting. That figure is telemetry, not time spent, and it is not specific to Mac.

A Forrester study commissioned by Microsoft reports 34.2% time savings in content creation for a modeled composite organization. It is an average across content tasks. It does not measure how long a finished deck takes you to review.
I did not find a Mac versus Windows speed benchmark for PowerPoint. If speed matters for your deck, test your own large file on your own Mac, and time the save.
Where Lazur fits in a PowerPoint session

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where a control is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it.

Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click, and you do the clicking. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app, including your speaker notes.
Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It returns a summary and a report. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, on your Mac.

items: Set the master, then save a template with File > Save as Template.
Build the layouts in one master, and count at least 15 of them.
Write the claims first, one per slide, with a source line in the master footer.

Check every SVG graphic, then test the file on an older version if it goes outside your team.
Press ⌘P, save a PDF, and send that PDF to the reviewers.

blocks.text: Ask Lazur to walk you through any step you forget. It circles the control and waits for your click.
Five mistakes that cost analysts time in PowerPoint

items: Building on the default master, then changing fonts slide by slide.
Expecting Designer to suggest layouts for chart and table slides.
Pasting charts as pictures, so the numbers cannot be checked or updated.
Reviewing the deck only on screen, and never as a printed or PDF copy.
Quoting vendor percentages as proof that your own deck got faster.

faq.question: Does PowerPoint for Mac have a keyboard shortcut for Slide Master?
faq.answer: Microsoft's Mac steps for Slide Master use the View tab and the Slide Master tab, and they list no keyboard shortcut. Open it from View > Slide Master. Third-party shortcut lists exist, but test any shortcut yourself before you rely on it.

faq.question: How many layouts does Designer need in a custom template?
faq.answer: Microsoft says Designer support for custom templates requires at least 15 layouts in each slide master. Designer only suggests layouts from the master a slide uses, so keep related layouts together in one master.

faq.question: Why does Designer not suggest anything for my chart slide?
faq.answer: Microsoft says Designer does not yet suggest designs for slides with tables or charts. Lay those slides out by hand, using a title only layout and the source line in the master footer.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my PowerPoint slides?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides, points, explains, answers out loud, and drafts or types text when you ask. It does not click buttons or edit files for you. You make every change in the deck yourself.

faq.question: Is the July 2026 reduced functionality mode still in effect?
faq.answer: I did not verify whether Microsoft's July 13, 2026 notice is still in effect. Read the known-issues page on the day you work. Ask your IT team if your Mac can open a file but cannot save it.

faq.question: Which PowerPoint for Mac build should I use?
faq.answer: Microsoft's release notes list 16.114.3, build 26102720, dated October 27, 2026, as the latest build I checked. Update through Microsoft AutoUpdate or your administrator, and check the release notes for newer builds.

faq.question: Does Copilot in PowerPoint for Mac cost extra?
faq.answer: Microsoft's release notes say Copilot in PowerPoint, added in version 16.109 on May 12, 2026, is available with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic). The notes do not list prices, so check Microsoft's pricing for your plan.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with PowerPoint on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on the Mac, on Apple silicon and Intel models. Windows is planned, not available. Use Lazur only on a Mac for now.
